title: Notification Delivery Service
summary: Send email, SMS, and push notifications reliably on behalf of other services.
statement:
Design a shared notification service that other teams call to notify users.

Functional requirements:
- Channels: mobile push, email, and SMS.
- Callers send an event and a template; the service fills in user details and preferences.
- Users can opt out per channel and per category, and set quiet hours.
- Some notifications are scheduled for a future time.
- Callers can see whether each notification was delivered.

Scale to assume:
- 1 billion notifications per day, with marketing campaigns causing spikes ten times the average.
- Security alerts such as password resets must go out within seconds even during a campaign.
hints: Third-party providers are slow and sometimes down. How do you keep that from blocking callers?
Retries can send the same message twice. What would you store to prevent duplicates?
How do you keep a large marketing campaign from delaying a password reset?
expectations: Clarifies channels, priorities, preferences and opt-outs, templating, scheduling, and delivery tracking requirements.
Estimates average and peak send rates and provider rate limits per channel.
Accepts requests through an API that validates and enqueues, then processes asynchronously with per-channel worker pools.
Separates queues or priorities so critical notifications are isolated from bulk campaigns.
Uses idempotency keys and a delivery log to avoid duplicates under retries, with exponential backoff and dead-letter queues.
Checks user preferences, quiet hours, and per-user frequency caps before sending.
Tracks provider callbacks for delivery status and supports provider failover.
